![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14261267/assets/52cce4fa3e48a0d44ff5fade12cb65f11614cfccc391cc3b11328e0aa58946b8.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $y=16x-16{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3}$ and the $x$-axis, shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}16x-16{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3} & =0 \\ 4x({x}^{2}-4x+4) & =0 \\ 4x(x-2)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=2.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x(16x-16{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(16{x}^{2}-16{x}^{3}+4{x}^{4})\text{d}x \\  & =8\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(4{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3}+{x}^{4})\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$
